transcript.text: Samsung WD90T534DBW washer dryer - clothes are still damp at the end of the wash and dry programme. It's not that old. Is the heater going?

To answer your question directly: it is possible the heater has failed, but that is actually one of the less common causes. Most often, a Samsung washer-dryer leaves clothes damp because of airflow issues (blocked filters/condenser), incorrect loading, or simply because the machine didn't spin the water out effectively before drying started. Before we suspect any parts, please check these two things:
1. Load size: Did you dry a full wash load? Washer-dryers can only dry about half of what they wash (e.g., 5kg dry max for an 8/9kg machine). If the load was too big, no amount of heating will fix it.
2. Spin quality: When the cycle ended, were the clothes soaking wet/dripping, or just damp? If they are dripping, the issue is likely with the spin/drain phase (pump filter blockage), not the heater. Please let me know if the load was within the dry capacity and how wet the clothes felt at the end.
It's a full 9kg drum, washes and dries in one go. The manual says 6kg dry. Clothes aren't dripping, just hot and damp at the end, towels and jeans worst. I sometimes turn the spin down to 800 too.

That suggests it: a full 9kg load is far too much for drying. The manual's 6kg limit is correct, but even that is optimistic; for thick items like towels and jeans, you really need to split them into smaller loads (around 4-5kg max). If you dry a full load, the centre stays wet regardless of how hot it gets. The other common cause for damp clothes when heat is present is restricted airflow—fluff blocking the lint filter or condenser prevents moisture from escaping. 1. Clean the lint filter (usually behind a small flap at the bottom front) and, if your model has one, the condenser unit (often near the door seal). Make sure they are clear of fluff.
2. Next time you dry, try putting in only about half the load (max 4-5kg) and set the spin to its highest setting (1400 or similar) before starting the drying programme. If it still leaves clothes damp after cleaning the filters and using a smaller load with high spin, we can look at other causes.
Tried a half drum with full spin and it came out dry, so it looks like I've just been overloading it. Is there anything else I should do apart from splitting the loads?

That is excellent news. It suggests the machine itself is fine and it was simply a case of trying to dry too much at once. To keep it running well, here are two quick tips:
1. Always set the spin speed as high as possible (e.g., 1400 or 1600) before starting the drying programme. The drier the clothes are when they go in, the better and faster the dryer will work.
2. Clean the lint filter every time you dry a load. It takes ten seconds but keeps the airflow clear so the machine doesn't have to work as hard. If you ever do get damp clothes again despite following those steps, just let me know. Otherwise, you should be good to go.
